name: Girth Pillar

days.note: Hike in via Mountaineer Creek to a bivy positioned between the two glaciers, allowing an early start up the Ice Cliff the next morning.
days.title: Approach to a bivy between the glaciers
days.objective: Reach a bivy in the scree between the Sherpa and Ice Cliff glaciers

days.note: In good conditions the Ice Cliff Glacier can be soloed to the base of the pillar in under 2 hours; the pillar itself offers 11 pitches with a crux of sustained crack climbing (~5.9) before easier ground leads to the summit ridge.
days.title: Climb the Ice Cliff Glacier and Girth Pillar to the summit

schedule.label: Climb the Ice Cliff Glacier to the base of the pillar
Top out near the summit ridge
Descend the Sherpa Glacier to camp and hike out

days.objective: Climb the glacier to the base of the pillar, then the pillar's 11 pitches to the summit

itinerary.totalNote: A 2-day rock route above the Ice Cliff Glacier: 11 pitches and ~6,000 ft gain over ~15 mi round trip; strong parties occasionally link it car-to-car.

approach: From the Stuart Lake Trailhead (Trail #1599, ~3,540') off Icicle Creek Rd/FS-7601, follow the Mountaineer Creek trail roughly 2.5 miles past the Colchuck Lake junction (~4,600'), then leave the trail before it climbs to Stuart Lake: ford Mountaineer Creek's south fork and climb steepening talus and heather benches directly toward the basin beneath the Ice Cliff Glacier on Stuart's northeast face (moraine camps around 6,800-7,000'). This off-trail stretch is loose and exposed to rockfall — expect real route-finding, especially in the dark on an alpine start. From camp, rope up and climb the Ice Cliff Glacier itself: this is the route's main objective hazard, with significant icefall, spindrift, and crevasse danger — parties typically stay left to dodge falling ice and swing wide right to avoid the glacier's largest crevasses. At the top of the glacier is the 'ice cliff' step itself, anywhere from 10 to 100+ feet of 50-70° snow/ice (easier and shorter early season, steeper and more likely bare ice as the season progresses). Above the step, four moderate pitches of rock lead to the base of the Girth Pillar proper (~8,200-8,400'). There is no water source above the moraine camp — carry what you need for the climb, or plan to melt snow/ice.

approach_logistics.trailheadDirection: From the Stuart Lake Trailhead (end of FR-7601 off Icicle Creek Road, ~3,540 ft), via the Mountaineer Creek drainage

descent_text: Girth Pillar is climbed in three sustained crack pitches above the four approach pitches: a steep P1 handcrack (5.10), a P2 crux of thin fingers and finger-locks (5.11-), and a P3 of sustained hands (5.10+), topping out on easier ground leading to the false summit above the Ice Cliff Glacier and on to Stuart's true summit. There is no reasonable way to reverse the route — down-climbing or rappelling back through the Ice Cliff Glacier's icefall and crevasse hazard is considerably more dangerous than finishing over the top, so continuing to the summit is effectively mandatory. From the true summit, retrace toward the false summit and descend the Sherpa Glacier, entered just east of where the Ice Cliff Glacier couloir tops out near 8,200 ft, back to the moraine camp; later in the season, once the Sherpa has melted out, parties go around Sherpa Peak to Sherpa Pass instead. Then walk out the Mountaineer Creek climbers' trail to the Stuart Lake trailhead, the same one used for the approach, so no car shuttle is needed. The glacier descent is technical, especially in the dark, so keep the axe, crampons and crevasse kit for it. If a party needs to bail from partway up the pillar itself, the crack pitches would need to be rappelled on natural gear anchors (no fixed hardware is reported on the pillar) — a real possibility to plan for given the route's commitment, but not part of the standard descent.
